---
title: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies
feature_id: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
rp1_run_id: caa0e3fa-4dc6-4dc4-a150-6f5d51856fba
status: approved
created: 2026-04-15
---

## Overview

Enable the rp1-eval-project CLI to validate YAML files using built-in Bun capabilities without introducing external dependencies. This feature extends the utility command set to support basic YAML syntax validation as a standalone command-line operation.

## Business Requirements

### REQ-001: YAML Validation Command (Must Have)

**Actor**: Developer / CLI User
**Action**: Execute a CLI command to validate YAML file syntax
**Outcome**: The command reports whether a YAML file is syntactically valid or identifies specific parsing errors
**Rationale**: YAML is a common configuration format; built-in validation eliminates configuration errors without adding package dependencies
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Command accepts a file path as argument
- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML
- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML
- Provides human-readable error messages on validation failure
- Produces minimal or no output on successful validation

### REQ-002: No External Dependency Introduction (Must Have)

**Actor**: Project Maintainer
**Action**: Implement YAML validation using only Bun standard library and built-in TypeScript parsing capabilities
**Outcome**: Project dependencies remain unchanged; no new packages added to package.json
**Rationale**: Keeps project lightweight and reduces supply-chain risk; maintains current minimal dependency footprint
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- No changes to devDependencies or dependencies in package.json
- Solution uses only Bun built-ins or native TypeScript/JavaScript parsing
- Code integrates with existing utility module structure

### REQ-003: Integration with Existing CLI (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Invoke YAML validation alongside existing utilities
**Outcome**: YAML validator is discoverable and accessible from the main entry point or CLI dispatch mechanism
**Rationale**: Consistent command interface improves usability and maintainability
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Can be invoked via a command-line argument or script
- Fits within existing project structure (utils.ts or index.ts pattern)
- Documentation or help text clarifies how to use the command

### REQ-004: Error Reporting (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer debugging YAML configuration
**Action**: Run validator on a malformed YAML file
**Outcome**: Receives clear indication of error location and nature
**Rationale**: Reduces debugging time and improves developer experience
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Error messages indicate line number (if possible)
- Error messages explain why the YAML is invalid
- Output distinguishes between parse errors and file-not-found errors

--- rp1_run_id: caa0e3fa-4dc6-4dc4-a150-6f5d51856fba --- # Design: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies **Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps **Version**: 1.0.0 **Status**: Draft **Created**: 2026-04-15 ## 1. Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts
(Command dispatch)"] end subgraph Utils["Utilities Layer"] Parser["yaml-parser.ts
(Minimal YAML parser)"] Validator["validateYaml()
(Validator wrapper)"] end subgraph Runtime["Bun Runtime"] FileIO["Bun.file()
(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Technology Stack | Layer | Technology | Rationale | |-------|-----------|-----------| | Runtime | Bun | Already required; no new dependency | | Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Project standard | | File I/O | Bun.file() | Built-in, simpler than Node fs for text files | | Parsing | Hand-written state machine | Zero dependencies; sufficient for common YAML | | Testing | Bun test (describe/test/expect) | Existing pattern in project | ## 5. Implementation Plan | # | Component | Description | Files Changed | |---|-----------|-------------|---------------| | T1 | YAML Parser | Hand-written minimal YAML parser with tokenization and tree building | `src/yaml-parser.ts` (new) | | T2 | Validator Wrapper | Export `validateYaml()` function integrating parser and file I/O | `src/utils.ts` (add function) | | T3 | CLI Dispatcher | Add command routing for `validate-yaml` argument in main entry point | `src/index.ts` (update) | | T4 | Unit Tests (Parser) | Test parser on valid YAML, common errors, edge cases | `src/yaml-parser.test.ts` (new) | | T5 | Integration Tests (CLI) | Test full CLI command with various YAML files | `src/index.test.ts` (new) | ## 6. Implementation DAG **Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies): 1. [T1, T4] - Parser implementation and unit tests can develop in parallel (tests validate parser immediately) **Dependencies**: - T2 -> T1 (Wrapper depends on parser: needs `parseYaml()` function exported) - T3 -> T2 (CLI dispatcher depends on validator: needs `validateYaml()` function) - T4 -> T1 (Unit tests import parser; can run once T1 exports function signature) - T5 -> T3 (Integration tests depend on CLI command being routable) **Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T5 ## 7. Testing Strategy ### Test Value Assessment | Valuable (design for) | Avoid (do NOT design for) | |-----------------------|--------------------------| | Parser correctness on valid YAML | JavaScript string methods behavior | | Parser error detection and reporting | Bun file I/O implementation details | | CLI command routing and exit codes | Exact error message wording (implementation detail) | | File-not-found handling | Deep YAML spec compliance (out of scope) | | Common configuration patterns (objects, lists, nesting) | Full YAML language feature coverage | ### Test Plan | Test | Type | What it verifies | |------|------|------------------| | Parse simple key-value | unit | Parser handles flat objects correctly | | Parse nested objects | unit | Indentation-based nesting works (key requirement) | | Parse lists | unit | Array syntax (- item) parsed correctly | | Parse comments | unit | Comment lines are ignored without error | | Parse quoted strings | unit | Quoted values preserve spaces and special chars | | Parse mixed types | unit | Type inference (numbers, booleans, null) works | | Detect indentation error | unit | Parser reports error on inconsistent indentation | | Detect invalid key-value syntax | unit | Parser reports error on malformed lines | | Depth limit | unit | Parser stops at max nesting (20 levels) | | CLI valid file | integration | Command returns exit 0 for valid YAML | | CLI invalid file | integration | Command returns exit 1 and prints error | | CLI file not found | integration | Command returns exit 2 and appropriate message | | CLI help/usage | integration | Help text available (if --help flag added) | ## 8. Deployment Design **Rollout Strategy**: 1. Implement and test in feature branch 2. Merge to main once all tests pass 3. No runtime migration or user action required 4. Feature is opt-in (only used when user explicitly calls `validate-yaml` command) **Backward Compatibility**: - Existing CLI behavior (entry point with single argument) unchanged - New functionality only activates with `validate-yaml` as first argument - No changes to existing utilities (greet, add functions) **Rollback**: - If parser has bugs discovered in production: revert commit - Feature is isolated; no impact on other functionality ## 9. Documentation Impact | Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale | |------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------| | add | README.md | New "CLI Commands" section | patterns.md | Document new validate-yaml command usage | | add | src/yaml-parser.ts | Module JSDoc | patterns.md | Explain parser scope and limitations | | add | src/utils.ts | validateYaml() JSDoc | patterns.md | Document function signature and error handling | | add | USAGE.md or docs/ | YAML Validation Guide | index.md | User guide with examples of valid/invalid YAML | ## 10. Design Decisions Log | ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered | |----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------| | D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written state machine (no regex) | Regex alone cannot handle indentation-dependent structure; state machine gives us full control and clear error messages | Regex-based, full YAML library (violates no-deps requirement) | | D2 | Parser scope | Support common config YAML; skip anchors, tags, advanced features | 80/20 rule: common config files use ~20% of YAML spec; advanced features rarely needed | Full YAML spec compliance (over-engineered for requirements) | | D3 | Error reporting | Include line number and context | Helps users debug quickly; critical for UX | Generic "invalid YAML" message | | D4 | Type inference | Basic (string, number, boolean, null) | Matches common config patterns; user can quote to force string | No type inference, return all as strings | | D5 | Depth limit | Max 20 levels of nesting | Prevents stack overflow; typical configs are 5-10 levels | Unlimited nesting (security/performance risk) | | D6 | File I/O | Bun.file() | Simple, built-in, matches project stack | Node fs (requires wrapping), Node path (extra cognitive load) | | D7 | CLI command | `validate-yaml` (kebab-case) | Matches project naming convention (patterns.md) | Other names (validateYaml, validate_yaml) | | D8 | Exit codes | 0 (success), 1 (parse error), 2 (file error) | Standard Unix convention; clear semantics | All errors return 1, or all non-zero |

# Design Decisions: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
**Created**: 2026-04-15

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written state machine (tokenization + tree building, no regex) | Regex alone cannot reliably handle indentation-dependent YAML structure; a state machine gives us full control, predictable error detection, and clear line-number reporting. Avoids external dependencies while maintaining correctness for ~80% of real-world config YAML. | Regex-based parser (fragile indentation handling); Full YAML library (violates "no new deps" requirement); Naive string splitting (poor error messages) |
| D2 | Parser feature scope | Support common configuration YAML; skip YAML 1.2 anchors, aliases, tags, and advanced features | Real-world config files (Kubernetes, Docker Compose, CI/CD) use a small subset of YAML. Supporting 20% of spec handles 80% of use cases. Clear documentation of scope prevents user confusion. | Full YAML spec compliance (over-engineered, adds complexity); Minimal parser (too limited, errors on valid configs) |
| D3 | Error reporting granularity | Report line number, column, and context line | Users debugging YAML errors need precise location to fix quickly. Matching editor line numbers (1-indexed) is standard. Showing the problematic line provides immediate feedback. | Generic error "Invalid YAML at token X" (poor UX); Stack trace only (confusing for non-developers) |
| D4 | Type inference strategy | Basic types: string (default), number, boolean, null; users can quote to force string | Matches configuration file patterns where most values are strings. Users familiar with YAML expect basic type coercion. Explicit quoting is standard for forcing string type. | No type inference, return all as strings (loses semantic information); Full YAML type inference (unnecessary complexity) |
| D5 | Nesting depth limit | Maximum 20 levels of nesting | Typical configuration files are 3-10 levels deep. 20-level limit is conservative and prevents stack overflow attacks or accidental deep nesting. Aligns with common practice in parsers. | No limit (DoS risk); Very low limit like 5 (blocks valid configs) |
| D6 | File I/O mechanism | Bun.file() with text encoding | Bun is the project runtime; Bun.file() is simpler than Node fs for single-file reads. No extra dependencies. Consistent with project tech stack. | Node fs (requires extra wrapping); fs.readFileSync (direct but requires import path); Deno API (different runtime) |
| D7 | CLI command naming | `validate-yaml` (kebab-case) | Matches project naming convention defined in patterns.md (kebab-case for CLI commands). Descriptive and verb-first. | `validateYaml`, `validate_yaml`, `yaml`, `check-yaml` (inconsistent with pattern or unclear) |
| D8 | Exit code semantics | 0 (success), 1 (parse error), 2 (file not found) | Standard Unix convention: 0 = success, non-zero = failure. Distinguishing file errors (2) from parse errors (1) allows users to script different recovery paths. | All non-zero (loses information); All errors return 1 (difficult to distinguish causes) |
| D9 | CLI output on success | Minimal: single line "YAML is valid" | Follows Unix philosophy (silence is golden). Users expect quiet success. Error case gets verbose output. Matches pattern of other validators. | Verbose output (noisy on valid files); JSON output (over-engineered for single command) |
| D10 | Module structure | New file `src/yaml-parser.ts` for parser; add `validateYaml()` to `src/utils.ts` | Separation of concerns: parser is a distinct capability. Utils.ts remains lightweight entry point for validation. Mirrors existing codebase structure. | All in utils.ts (mixing levels of abstraction); All in index.ts (bloats entry point) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Parser implementation language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing codebase pattern | Project standard; all source in TypeScript; benefits from type checking |
| File reading | Bun.file() API | Bun is project runtime | Zero-dependency file I/O; async-friendly but sync acceptable for CLI |
| Test framework | Bun's built-in test runner (describe/test/expect) | Existing test pattern in utils.test.ts | Project already uses this; no external dependencies; matches existing test structure |
| Error object structure | Custom interface (message, line, column, context) | Conservative pattern | Avoids external error libraries; simple, predictable, serializable |
| CLI parsing | process.argv direct access | Existing pattern in index.ts | No external CLI parser library; matches current simple routing |
| Module exports | Named exports in utils.ts and yaml-parser.ts | Project convention | ESM modules with explicit named functions; type-safe with TypeScript |

# Hypothesis Document: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Created**: 2026-04-15 | **Status**: PENDING

## Hypotheses

### HYP-001: Indentation-based YAML parsing without regex is feasible
**Risk Level**: HIGH
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: A hand-written state machine parser can reliably detect and report indentation errors in YAML without using regex for indentation validation.
**Context**: The design relies on a state machine tracking indentation levels to build nested objects. If indentation context-sensitivity proves too complex, the parser will produce incorrect parse trees or miss error cases, leading to invalid YAML being accepted or valid YAML being rejected.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Prototype parser correctly parses common config patterns (nested objects, lists, mixed) and rejects files with inconsistent indentation (mixing spaces/tabs, incorrect levels)
- REJECT if: Prototype fails to detect indentation errors, produces incorrect parse trees for nested structures, or mishandles edge cases like trailing/leading whitespace
**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT

### HYP-002: Bun.file() API supports the required text file operations for a CLI validator
**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: Bun.file() provides text reading capability that integrates seamlessly with our parser (can read entire file as string with proper encoding handling).
**Context**: The design assumes Bun.file() will handle text files efficiently. If Bun.file() requires special handling or lacks features we expect, we may need to fall back to alternative I/O mechanisms or rethink the approach.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Bun.file().text() works as documented, handles UTF-8 encoding transparently, and throws appropriate errors for missing files
- REJECT if: API is missing, requires workarounds, or has unexpected behavior (e.g., binary-only mode)
**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT

### HYP-003: A minimal YAML parser covering ~80% of real-world config YAML is sufficient for the use case
**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: The proposed feature scope (key-value, nesting, lists, comments, basic types) covers the majority of YAML used in configuration files; advanced features (anchors, tags, aliases) are rarely needed.
**Context**: If users frequently encounter advanced YAML features and expect validation for them, the limited parser will frustrate users and reduce feature adoption. Conversely, if most configs are simple, the design is perfectly fit.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Testing on 5-10 real-world config files (Kubernetes manifests, Docker Compose, CI/CD files) shows the parser correctly validates them without skipping advanced features
- REJECT if: Multiple test files fail validation due to missing advanced feature support, or documentation requests indicate demand for features we don't support
**Suggested Method**: EXTERNAL_RESEARCH (review real-world config examples)

- **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing
- **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference

# Development Tasks: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps

**Status**: Not Started

**Progress**: 0% (0 of 9 tasks)

**Estimated Effort**: 5 days

## Overview

This feature adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies.

The approach prioritizes:
- **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing
- **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference
- **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging
- **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern

## Overview

Enable the rp1-eval-project CLI to validate YAML files using built-in Bun capabilities without introducing external dependencies. This feature extends the utility command set to support basic YAML syntax validation as a standalone command-line operation.

## Business Requirements

### REQ-001: YAML Validation Command (Must Have)

**Actor**: Developer / CLI User
**Action**: Execute a CLI command to validate YAML file syntax
**Outcome**: The command reports whether a YAML file is syntactically valid or identifies specific parsing errors
**Rationale**: YAML is a common configuration format; built-in validation eliminates configuration errors without adding package dependencies
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Command accepts a file path as argument
- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML
- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML
- Provides human-readable error messages on validation failure
- Produces minimal or no output on successful validation

### REQ-002: No External Dependency Introduction (Must Have)

**Actor**: Project Maintainer
**Action**: Implement YAML validation using only Bun standard library and built-in TypeScript parsing capabilities
**Outcome**: Project dependencies remain unchanged; no new packages added to package.json
**Rationale**: Keeps project lightweight and reduces supply-chain risk; maintains current minimal dependency footprint
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- No changes to devDependencies or dependencies in package.json
- Solution uses only Bun built-ins or native TypeScript/JavaScript parsing
- Code integrates with existing utility module structure

### REQ-003: Integration with Existing CLI (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Invoke YAML validation alongside existing utilities
**Outcome**: YAML validator is discoverable and accessible from the main entry point or CLI dispatch mechanism
**Rationale**: Consistent command interface improves usability and maintainability
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Can be invoked via a command-line argument or script
- Fits within existing project structure (utils.ts or index.ts pattern)
- Documentation or help text clarifies how to use the command

### REQ-004: Error Reporting (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer debugging YAML configuration
**Action**: Run validator on a malformed YAML file
**Outcome**: Receives clear indication of error location and nature
**Rationale**: Reduces debugging time and improves developer experience
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Error messages indicate line number (if possible)
- Error messages explain why the YAML is invalid
- Output distinguishes between parse errors and file-not-found errors

## Scope

**Included**:
- YAML syntax validation using Bun built-ins
- Command-line interface for file validation
- Error messages and exit code signaling
- Integration with existing utils module

**Not Included**:
- JSON Schema validation or semantic YAML analysis
- External YAML library dependencies
- GUI or interactive validation mode
- Performance benchmarking or large-file optimization
- Configuration for YAML dialect variants

## Success Criteria

- Feature can be invoked as a new CLI command
- Validates YAML syntax without external libraries
- Provides actionable error feedback
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Feature is documented with usage examples

## Dependencies & Constraints

- Must use Bun standard library or native JavaScript/TypeScript parsing
- Cannot add npm dependencies
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing code
- Must follow existing project code patterns and conventions

Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts
(Command dispatch)"] end subgraph Utils["Utilities Layer"] Parser["yaml-parser.ts
(Minimal YAML parser)"] Validator["validateYaml()
(Validator wrapper)"] end subgraph Runtime["Bun Runtime"] FileIO["Bun.file()
(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts

Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. # Development Tasks: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps

**Status**: In Progress

**Progress**: 11% (1 of 9 tasks)

**Estimated Effort**: 5 days

**Started**: 2026-04-15

## Overview

This feature adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies.

The approach prioritizes:
- **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing
- **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference
- **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging
- **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1, T4] - Parser implementation and unit tests can develop in parallel (tests validate parser immediately)

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Wrapper depends on parser: needs `parseYaml()` function exported)
- T3 -> T2 (CLI dispatcher depends on validator: needs `validateYaml()` function)
- T4 -> T1 (Unit tests import parser; can run once T1 exports function signature)
- T5 -> T3 (Integration tests depend on CLI command being routable)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T5

Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts

(Validator wrapper)"] end subgraph Runtime["Bun Runtime"] FileIO["Bun.file()
(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. title: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies
feature_id: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
rp1_run_id: caa0e3fa-4dc6-4dc4-a150-6f5d51856fba

## Overview

Enable the rp1-eval-project CLI to validate YAML files using built-in Bun capabilities without introducing external dependencies. This feature extends the utility command set to support basic YAML syntax validation as a standalone command-line operation.

## Business Requirements

### REQ-001: YAML Validation Command (Must Have)

**Actor**: Developer / CLI User
**Action**: Execute a CLI command to validate YAML file syntax
**Outcome**: The command reports whether a YAML file is syntactically valid or identifies specific parsing errors
**Rationale**: YAML is a common configuration format; built-in validation eliminates configuration errors without adding package dependencies
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Command accepts a file path as argument
- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML
- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML
- Provides human-readable error messages on validation failure
- Produces minimal or no output on successful validation

### REQ-002: No External Dependency Introduction (Must Have)

**Actor**: Project Maintainer
**Action**: Implement YAML validation using only Bun standard library and built-in TypeScript parsing capabilities
**Outcome**: Project dependencies remain unchanged; no new packages added to package.json
**Rationale**: Keeps project lightweight and reduces supply-chain risk; maintains current minimal dependency footprint
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- No changes to devDependencies or dependencies in package.json
- Solution uses only Bun built-ins or native TypeScript/JavaScript parsing
- Code integrates with existing utility module structure

### REQ-003: Integration with Existing CLI (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Invoke YAML validation alongside existing utilities
**Outcome**: YAML validator is discoverable and accessible from the main entry point or CLI dispatch mechanism
**Rationale**: Consistent command interface improves usability and maintainability
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Can be invoked via a command-line argument or script
- Fits within existing project structure (utils.ts or index.ts pattern)
- Documentation or help text clarifies how to use the command

### REQ-004: Error Reporting (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer debugging YAML configuration
**Action**: Run validator on a malformed YAML file
**Outcome**: Receives clear indication of error location and nature
**Rationale**: Reduces debugging time and improves developer experience
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Error messages indicate line number (if possible)
- Error messages explain why the YAML is invalid
- Output distinguishes between parse errors and file-not-found errors

## Scope

**Included**:
- YAML syntax validation using Bun built-ins
- Command-line interface for file validation
- Error messages and exit code signaling
- Integration with existing utils module

**Not Included**:
- JSON Schema validation or semantic YAML analysis
- External YAML library dependencies
- GUI or interactive validation mode
- Performance benchmarking or large-file optimization
- Configuration for YAML dialect variants

## Success Criteria

- Feature can be invoked as a new CLI command
- Validates YAML syntax without external libraries
- Provides actionable error feedback
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Feature is documented with usage examples

## Dependencies & Constraints

- Must use Bun standard library or native JavaScript/TypeScript parsing
- Cannot add npm dependencies
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing code
- Must follow existing project code patterns and conventions

--- rp1_run_id: caa0e3fa-4dc6-4dc4-a150-6f5d51856fba --- # Design: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies **Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps **Version**: 1.0.0 **Status**: Draft **Created**: 2026-04-15 ## 1. Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts
(Command dispatch)"] end subgraph Utils["Utilities Layer"] Parser["yaml-parser.ts
(Minimal YAML parser)"] Validator["validateYaml()
(Validator wrapper)"] end subgraph Runtime["Bun Runtime"] FileIO["Bun.file()
(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. # Design Decisions: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
**Created**: 2026-04-15

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written state machine (tokenization + tree building, no regex) | Regex alone cannot reliably handle indentation-dependent YAML structure; a state machine gives us full control, predictable error detection, and clear line-number reporting. Avoids external dependencies while maintaining correctness for ~80% of real-world config YAML. | Regex-based parser (fragile indentation handling); Full YAML library (violates "no new deps" requirement); Naive string splitting (poor error messages) |
| D2 | Parser feature scope | Support common configuration YAML; skip YAML 1.2 anchors, aliases, tags, and advanced features | Real-world config files (Kubernetes, Docker Compose, CI/CD) use a small subset of YAML. Supporting 20% of spec handles 80% of use cases. Clear documentation of scope prevents user confusion. | Full YAML spec compliance (over-engineered, adds complexity); Minimal parser (too limited, errors on valid configs) |
| D3 | Error reporting granularity | Report line number, column, and context line | Users debugging YAML errors need precise location to fix quickly. Matching editor line numbers (1-indexed) is standard. Showing the problematic line provides immediate feedback. | Generic error "Invalid YAML at token X" (poor UX); Stack trace only (confusing for non-developers) |
| D4 | Type inference strategy | Basic types: string (default), number, boolean, null; users can quote to force string | Matches configuration file patterns where most values are strings. Users familiar with YAML expect basic type coercion. Explicit quoting is standard for forcing string type. | No type inference, return all as strings (loses semantic information); Full YAML type inference (unnecessary complexity) |
| D5 | Nesting depth limit | Maximum 20 levels of nesting | Typical configuration files are 3-10 levels deep. 20-level limit is conservative and prevents stack overflow attacks or accidental deep nesting. Aligns with common practice in parsers. | No limit (DoS risk); Very low limit like 5 (blocks valid configs) |
| D6 | File I/O mechanism | Bun.file() with text encoding | Bun is the project runtime; Bun.file() is simpler than Node fs for single-file reads. No extra dependencies. Consistent with project tech stack. | Node fs (requires extra wrapping); fs.readFileSync (direct but requires import path); Deno API (different runtime) |
| D7 | CLI command naming | `validate-yaml` (kebab-case) | Matches project naming convention defined in patterns.md (kebab-case for CLI commands). Descriptive and verb-first. | `validateYaml`, `validate_yaml`, `yaml`, `check-yaml` (inconsistent with pattern or unclear) |
| D8 | Exit code semantics | 0 (success), 1 (parse error), 2 (file not found) | Standard Unix convention: 0 = success, non-zero = failure. Distinguishing file errors (2) from parse errors (1) allows users to script different recovery paths. | All non-zero (loses information); All errors return 1 (difficult to distinguish causes) |
| D9 | CLI output on success | Minimal: single line "YAML is valid" | Follows Unix philosophy (silence is golden). Users expect quiet success. Error case gets verbose output. Matches pattern of other validators. | Verbose output (noisy on valid files); JSON output (over-engineered for single command) |
| D10 | Module structure | New file `src/yaml-parser.ts` for parser; add `validateYaml()` to `src/utils.ts` | Separation of concerns: parser is a distinct capability. Utils.ts remains lightweight entry point for validation. Mirrors existing codebase structure. | All in utils.ts (mixing levels of abstraction); All in index.ts (bloats entry point) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Parser implementation language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing codebase pattern | Project standard; all source in TypeScript; benefits from type checking |
| File reading | Bun.file() API | Bun is project runtime | Zero-dependency file I/O; async-friendly but sync acceptable for CLI |
| Test framework | Bun's built-in test runner (describe/test/expect) | Existing test pattern in utils.test.ts | Project already uses this; no external dependencies; matches existing test structure |
| Error object structure | Custom interface (message, line, column, context) | Conservative pattern | Avoids external error libraries; simple, predictable, serializable |
| CLI parsing | process.argv direct access | Existing pattern in index.ts | No external CLI parser library; matches current simple routing |
| Module exports | Named exports in utils.ts and yaml-parser.ts | Project convention | ESM modules with explicit named functions; type-safe with TypeScript |

# Hypothesis Document: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Created**: 2026-04-15 | **Status**: PENDING

## Hypotheses

### HYP-001: Indentation-based YAML parsing without regex is feasible
**Risk Level**: HIGH
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: A hand-written state machine parser can reliably detect and report indentation errors in YAML without using regex for indentation validation.
**Context**: The design relies on a state machine tracking indentation levels to build nested objects. If indentation context-sensitivity proves too complex, the parser will produce incorrect parse trees or miss error cases, leading to invalid YAML being accepted or valid YAML being rejected.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Prototype parser correctly parses common config patterns (nested objects, lists, mixed) and rejects files with inconsistent indentation (mixing spaces/tabs, incorrect levels)
- REJECT if: Prototype fails to detect indentation errors, produces incorrect parse trees for nested structures, or mishandles edge cases like trailing/leading whitespace
**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT

### HYP-002: Bun.file() API supports the required text file operations for a CLI validator
**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: Bun.file() provides text reading capability that integrates seamlessly with our parser (can read entire file as string with proper encoding handling).
**Context**: The design assumes Bun.file() will handle text files efficiently. If Bun.file() requires special handling or lacks features we expect, we may need to fall back to alternative I/O mechanisms or rethink the approach.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Bun.file().text() works as documented, handles UTF-8 encoding transparently, and throws appropriate errors for missing files
- REJECT if: API is missing, requires workarounds, or has unexpected behavior (e.g., binary-only mode)
**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT

### HYP-003: A minimal YAML parser covering ~80% of real-world config YAML is sufficient for the use case
**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
**Status**: PENDING
**Statement**: The proposed feature scope (key-value, nesting, lists, comments, basic types) covers the majority of YAML used in configuration files; advanced features (anchors, tags, aliases) are rarely needed.
**Context**: If users frequently encounter advanced YAML features and expect validation for them, the limited parser will frustrate users and reduce feature adoption. Conversely, if most configs are simple, the design is perfectly fit.
**Validation Criteria**:
- CONFIRM if: Testing on 5-10 real-world config files (Kubernetes manifests, Docker Compose, CI/CD files) shows the parser correctly validates them without skipping advanced features
- REJECT if: Multiple test files fail validation due to missing advanced feature support, or documentation requests indicate demand for features we don't support
**Suggested Method**: EXTERNAL_RESEARCH (review real-world config examples)

# Development Tasks: Add Simple YAML Validator Command Without Adding New Dependencies

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps

**Status**: Not Started

**Progress**: 0% (0 of 9 tasks)

**Estimated Effort**: 5 days

**Started**: 2026-04-15

## Overview

This feature adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies.

The approach prioritizes:
- **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing
- **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference
- **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging
- **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1, T4] - Parser implementation and unit tests can develop in parallel (tests validate parser immediately)

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Wrapper depends on parser: needs `parseYaml()` function exported)
- T3 -> T2 (CLI dispatcher depends on validator: needs `validateYaml()` function)
- T4 -> T1 (Unit tests import parser; can run once T1 exports function signature)
- T5 -> T3 (Integration tests depend on CLI command being routable)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T5

stateDiagram-v2

    T3 --> T5
    T5 : T5: Integration tests
    T5 --> [*]
```

## Task Breakdown

### Parser & Unit Tests (Parallel Execution)

- [ ] **T1**: Implement hand-written YAML parser with tokenization and tree building `[complexity:complex]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#31-yaml-parser-implementation](design.md#31-yaml-parser-implementation)

    **Effort**: 8 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] New file `src/yaml-parser.ts` created with `parseYaml(content: string): ParseResult` function
    - [ ] Parser handles comments (lines starting with #)
    - [ ] Parser handles key-value pairs (key: value syntax)
    - [ ] Parser handles nested objects (indentation-based)
    - [ ] Parser handles lists (- item syntax)
    - [ ] Parser performs basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null)
    - [ ] Parser handles quoted strings and escape sequences
    - [ ] Parser detects indentation inconsistencies and reports errors with line/column
    - [ ] Parser enforces maximum nesting depth of 20 levels
    - [ ] ParseResult interface matches design spec (success bool, data/error union)
    - [ ] Error messages include line number, column, and context
    - [ ] No external dependencies used (only built-in JavaScript)

- [ ] **T4**: Write unit tests for YAML parser covering valid YAML and error cases `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#test-plan](design.md#test-plan)

    **Effort**: 6 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] New file `src/yaml-parser.test.ts` created with Bun test harness
    - [ ] Test: Parse simple key-value pairs
    - [ ] Test: Parse nested objects (indentation handling)

    - [ ] Test: Parse comments and blank lines
    - [ ] Test: Parse quoted strings (preserves spaces and special chars)
    - [ ] Test: Parse mixed types (strings, numbers, booleans, null)
    - [ ] Test: Detect indentation errors

### Core Integration (Sequential Chain)

- [ ] **T2**: Export `validateYaml()` function in utils.ts integrating parser and file I/O `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#32-data-model](design.md#32-data-model)

    **Effort**: 4 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Function `validateYaml(filePath: string): Promise<ParseResult>` exported from `src/utils.ts`
    - [ ] Function reads file using `Bun.file()` API
    - [ ] Function calls `parseYaml()` from yaml-parser.ts
    - [ ] Function handles file-not-found errors gracefully
    - [ ] Function returns structured ParseResult (success + data/error)
    - [ ] Error messages distinguish between file errors and parse errors
    - [ ] JSDoc comment explains function signature, parameters, return type, and error handling

- [ ] **T3**: Add CLI command routing for `validate-yaml` in index.ts `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#33-cli-integration](design.md#33-cli-integration)

    **Effort**: 2 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] `src/index.ts` detects `validate-yaml` command from `process.argv[2]`
    - [ ] File path argument is read from `process.argv[3]`
    - [ ] CLI calls `validateYaml()` with the provided file path
    - [ ] Exit code 0 on successful validation (prints "YAML is valid" or minimal output)
    - [ ] Exit code 1 on parse error (prints error details)
    - [ ] Exit code 2 on file-not-found error (prints appropriate message)
    - [ ] Help text is available or command is self-documenting

- [ ] **T5**: Write integration tests for full CLI command with various YAML files `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#test-plan](design.md#test-plan)

    - [ ] Tests validate exit codes and output format

**Status**: Not Started

## Overview

This feature adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies.

The approach prioritizes:
- **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing
- **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference
- **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging
- **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern

## Overview

Enable the rp1-eval-project CLI to validate YAML files using built-in Bun capabilities without introducing external dependencies. This feature extends the utility command set to support basic YAML syntax validation as a standalone command-line operation.

## Business Requirements

### REQ-001: YAML Validation Command (Must Have)

**Actor**: Developer / CLI User
**Action**: Execute a CLI command to validate YAML file syntax
**Outcome**: The command reports whether a YAML file is syntactically valid or identifies specific parsing errors
**Rationale**: YAML is a common configuration format; built-in validation eliminates configuration errors without adding package dependencies
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Command accepts a file path as argument
- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML
- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML
- Provides human-readable error messages on validation failure
- Produces minimal or no output on successful validation

### REQ-002: No External Dependency Introduction (Must Have)

**Actor**: Project Maintainer
**Action**: Implement YAML validation using only Bun standard library and built-in TypeScript parsing capabilities
**Outcome**: Project dependencies remain unchanged; no new packages added to package.json
**Rationale**: Keeps project lightweight and reduces supply-chain risk; maintains current minimal dependency footprint
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- No changes to devDependencies or dependencies in package.json
- Solution uses only Bun built-ins or native TypeScript/JavaScript parsing
- Code integrates with existing utility module structure

### REQ-003: Integration with Existing CLI (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Invoke YAML validation alongside existing utilities
**Outcome**: YAML validator is discoverable and accessible from the main entry point or CLI dispatch mechanism
**Rationale**: Consistent command interface improves usability and maintainability
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Can be invoked via a command-line argument or script
- Fits within existing project structure (utils.ts or index.ts pattern)
- Documentation or help text clarifies how to use the command

### REQ-004: Error Reporting (Should Have)

**Actor**: Developer debugging YAML configuration
**Action**: Run validator on a malformed YAML file
**Outcome**: Receives clear indication of error location and nature
**Rationale**: Reduces debugging time and improves developer experience
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Error messages indicate line number (if possible)
- Error messages explain why the YAML is invalid
- Output distinguishes between parse errors and file-not-found errors

## Scope

**Included**:
- YAML syntax validation using Bun built-ins
- Command-line interface for file validation
- Error messages and exit code signaling
- Integration with existing utils module

**Not Included**:
- JSON Schema validation or semantic YAML analysis
- External YAML library dependencies
- GUI or interactive validation mode
- Performance benchmarking or large-file optimization
- Configuration for YAML dialect variants

## Success Criteria

- Feature can be invoked as a new CLI command
- Validates YAML syntax without external libraries
- Provides actionable error feedback
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Feature is documented with usage examples

## Dependencies & Constraints

- Must use Bun standard library or native JavaScript/TypeScript parsing
- Cannot add npm dependencies
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing code
- Must follow existing project code patterns and conventions

(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Technology Stack | Layer | Technology | Rationale | |-------|-----------|-----------| | Runtime | Bun | Already required; no new dependency | | Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Project standard | | File I/O | Bun.file() | Built-in, simpler than Node fs for text files | | Parsing | Hand-written state machine | Zero dependencies; sufficient for common YAML | | Testing | Bun test (describe/test/expect) | Existing pattern in project | ## 5. Deployment Design **Rollout Strategy**: 1. Implement and test in feature branch 2. Merge to main once all tests pass 3. No runtime migration or user action required 4. Feature is opt-in (only used when user explicitly calls `validate-yaml` command) **Backward Compatibility**: - Existing CLI behavior (entry point with single argument) unchanged - New functionality only activates with `validate-yaml` as first argument - No changes to existing utilities (greet, add functions) **Rollback**: - If parser has bugs discovered in production: revert commit - Feature is isolated; no impact on other functionality ## 9. Design Overview This design adds a lightweight YAML validation command to the rp1-eval-project CLI using only built-in Bun and TypeScript capabilities. The solution implements a minimal hand-written YAML parser that handles common configuration YAML syntax without external dependencies. The approach prioritizes: - **No new dependencies**: Uses only Bun's file I/O and native JavaScript parsing - **Common YAML coverage**: Supports key-value pairs, nested objects, lists, comments, basic type inference - **Clear error reporting**: Line-number-aware error messages for debugging - **Simple integration**: Fits naturally into existing utils module and CLI pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"] Index["index.ts
(Command dispatch)"] end subgraph Utils["Utilities Layer"] Parser["yaml-parser.ts
(Minimal YAML parser)"] Validator["validateYaml()
(Validator wrapper)"] end subgraph Runtime["Bun Runtime"] FileIO["Bun.file()
(File I/O)"] end Index -->|calls| Validator Validator -->|uses| Parser Parser -->|reads file| FileIO ``` ## 2. Architecture The architecture consists of three layers: **Layer 1: CLI Dispatcher (index.ts)** - Detects `validate-yaml` command from process.argv - Routes to the validator function with the file path argument - Handles exit codes and error output **Layer 2: Validator Wrapper (utils.ts)** - Exports `validateYaml(filePath: string)` function - Reads file using Bun.file() - Calls the parser and returns structured error information **Layer 3: YAML Parser (yaml-parser.ts - new)** - Implements a state-machine-based YAML parser - Handles: - Comments (lines starting with #) - Key-value pairs (key: value) - Nested objects (indentation-based) - Lists (- item syntax) - Basic type inference (strings, numbers, booleans, null) - Escaping and quoted strings - Returns parse tree or detailed error with line/column info - Depth limit: 20 levels (prevents stack overflow on pathological input) ## 3. Detailed Design ### 3.1 YAML Parser Implementation The parser uses a token-based approach with these phases: **Phase 1: Tokenization** - Split input into lines - Classify each line (comment, blank, key-value, list item, etc.) - Track indentation level for each line **Phase 2: Tree Building** - Use a stack to manage nested levels - When indentation increases, push new object/list - When indentation decreases, pop from stack - Detect indentation inconsistencies (error) **Phase 3: Value Parsing** - Parse right-hand side of key-value pairs - Handle quoted strings, escape sequences - Infer types: "123" → number, "true" → boolean, "null" → null - Default to string type **Error Reporting** - Track line and column for each token - Report first error encountered with full context - Example: `Line 5, Column 12: Invalid indentation (expected 2, got 3 spaces)` ### 3.2 Data Model ```typescript // Result of parsing interface ParseResult { success: boolean; data?: Record; error?: ParseError; } interface ParseError { message: string; line: number; column: number; context: string; // the problematic line } ``` ### 3.3 CLI Integration The CLI detects the validate-yaml command by checking `process.argv[2]`: ``` bun run src/index.ts validate-yaml path/to/file.yaml ``` On success: prints "YAML is valid" (or minimal output), exit code 0 On error: prints error details, exit code 1 On file not found: prints "File not found", exit code 2 ## 4. Technology Stack | Layer | Technology | Rationale | |-------|-----------|-----------| | Runtime | Bun | Already required; no new dependency | | Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Project standard | | File I/O | Bun.file() | Built-in, simpler than Node fs for text files | | Parsing | Hand-written state machine | Zero dependencies; sufficient for common YAML | | Testing | Bun test (describe/test/expect) | Existing pattern in project | ## 5. Implementation Plan | # | Component | Description | Files Changed | |---|-----------|-------------|---------------| | T1 | YAML Parser | Hand-written minimal YAML parser with tokenization and tree building | `src/yaml-parser.ts` (new) | | T2 | Validator Wrapper | Export `validateYaml()` function integrating parser and file I/O | `src/utils.ts` (add function) | | T3 | CLI Dispatcher | Add command routing for `validate-yaml` argument in main entry point | `src/index.ts` (update) | | T4 | Unit Tests (Parser) | Test parser on valid YAML, common errors, edge cases | `src/yaml-parser.test.ts` (new) | | T5 | Integration Tests (CLI) | Test full CLI command with various YAML files | `src/index.test.ts` (new) | ## 6. Implementation DAG **Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies): 1. [T1, T4] - Parser implementation and unit tests can develop in parallel (tests validate parser immediately) **Dependencies**: - T2 -> T1 (Wrapper depends on parser: needs `parseYaml()` function exported) - T3 -> T2 (CLI dispatcher depends on validator: needs `validateYaml()` function) - T4 -> T1 (Unit tests import parser; can run once T1 exports function signature) - T5 -> T3 (Integration tests depend on CLI command being routable) **Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T5 ## 7. Testing Strategy ### Test Value Assessment | Valuable (design for) | Avoid (do NOT design for) | |-----------------------|--------------------------| | Parser correctness on valid YAML | JavaScript string methods behavior | | Parser error detection and reporting | Bun file I/O implementation details | | CLI command routing and exit codes | Exact error message wording (implementation detail) | | File-not-found handling | Deep YAML spec compliance (out of scope) | | Common configuration patterns (objects, lists, nesting) | Full YAML language feature coverage | ### Test Plan | Test | Type | What it verifies | |------|------|------------------| | Parse simple key-value | unit | Parser handles flat objects correctly | | Parse nested objects | unit | Indentation-based nesting works (key requirement) | | Parse lists | unit | Array syntax (- item) parsed correctly | | Parse comments | unit | Comment lines are ignored without error | | Parse quoted strings | unit | Quoted values preserve spaces and special chars | | Parse mixed types | unit | Type inference (numbers, booleans, null) works | | Detect indentation error | unit | Parser reports error on inconsistent indentation | | Detect invalid key-value syntax | unit | Parser reports error on malformed lines | | Depth limit | unit | Parser stops at max nesting (20 levels) | | CLI valid file | integration | Command returns exit 0 for valid YAML | | CLI invalid file | integration | Command returns exit 1 and prints error | | CLI file not found | integration | Command returns exit 2 and appropriate message | | CLI help/usage | integration | Help text available (if --help flag added) | ## 8. Deployment Design **Rollout Strategy**: 1. Implement and test in feature branch 2. Merge to main once all tests pass 3. No runtime migration or user action required 4. Feature is opt-in (only used when user explicitly calls `validate-yaml` command) **Backward Compatibility**: - Existing CLI behavior (entry point with single argument) unchanged - New functionality only activates with `validate-yaml` as first argument - No changes to existing utilities (greet, add functions) **Rollback**: - If parser has bugs discovered in production: revert commit - Feature is isolated; no impact on other functionality ## 9. Documentation Impact | Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale | |------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------| | add | README.md | New "CLI Commands" section | patterns.md | Document new validate-yaml command usage | | add | src/yaml-parser.ts | Module JSDoc | patterns.md | Explain parser scope and limitations | | add | src/utils.ts | validateYaml() JSDoc | patterns.md | Document function signature and error handling | | add | USAGE.md or docs/ | YAML Validation Guide | index.md | User guide with examples of valid/invalid YAML | ## 10. Design Decisions Log | ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered | |----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------| | D1 | YAML parsing approach | Hand-written state machine (no regex) | Regex alone cannot handle indentation-dependent structure; state machine gives us full control and clear error messages | Regex-based, full YAML library (violates no-deps requirement) | | D2 | Parser scope | Support common config YAML; skip anchors, tags, advanced features | 80/20 rule: common config files use ~20% of YAML spec; advanced features rarely needed | Full YAML spec compliance (over-engineered for requirements) | | D3 | Error reporting | Include line number and context | Helps users debug quickly; critical for UX | Generic "invalid YAML" message | | D4 | Type inference | Basic (string, number, boolean, null) | Matches common config patterns; user can quote to force string | No type inference, return all as strings | | D5 | Depth limit | Max 20 levels of nesting | Prevents stack overflow; typical configs are 5-10 levels | Unlimited nesting (security/performance risk) | | D6 | File I/O | Bun.file() | Simple, built-in, matches project stack | Node fs (requires wrapping), Node path (extra cognitive load) | | D7 | CLI command | `validate-yaml` (kebab-case) | Matches project naming convention (patterns.md) | Other names (validateYaml, validate_yaml) | | D8 | Exit codes | 0 (success), 1 (parse error), 2 (file error) | Standard Unix convention; clear semantics | All errors return 1, or all non-zero |
